subject: Quick recap + procurement check — Redwood fit
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Grant <alicia@statelypay.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + procurement check — Redwood fit

Hi Alicia — great to meet earlier. Short recap and a couple of procurement/next-step questions so we can tailor pricing: 

Recap (30-min discovery)
- Primary use case: real-time personalization for transaction flows (token-level generation + embeddings)
- Target latency: <150ms p95 for text generation on peak flows
- Data controls: must retain logs 90 days, must support customer-managed KMS for keys
- Expected start footprint: pilot at ~100k monthly active events, scaling to ~1M within 12 months

Procurement + commercial clarifying Qs
1) Purchasing path: will finance process this via a PO (standard SOW/paper route) or is card/credit-card payment acceptable for initial pilot?
2) Marketplace: are you required/prefer to transact via AWS Marketplace or similar procurement channels?
3) Commit appetite: for Dedicated (reserved capacity) pricing we typically ask for a 12-month commit; is a commit possible or do you need on-demand first?

Next steps I propose:
- If PO/SOW: I’ll loop in our contracts lead with an initial MPA/term sheet and a draft SOW template (attached draft pricing summary).
- If card/on-demand: we can spin up a pilot on hosted API immediately and provide usage guidance and throttles.
- If marketplace required: I’ll confirm our AWS Marketplace SKU availability and procurement timeline.

Please reply with (a) PO vs card (b) marketplace requirement (yes/no) and (c) whether you can give a ballpark commit range if you’re open to Dedicated.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0114

Attachments: redwood-pricing-summary-nov2026.pdf (pricing overview, hosted vs dedicated vs private)
From: Alicia Grant <alicia@statelypay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureOps Team <procureops@statelypay.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement check — Redwood fit

Thanks Jordan — quick answers from procurement side: 

1) Purchasing path: StatelyPay prefers PO for any multi-month commitments; pilot purchases under $10k can be done on card, but anything above will require PO paperwork and a signed MPA.
2) Marketplace: We prefer Marketplace when projects are tied to a chargeback model to our internal cloud team, but it's not a hard blocker — it speeds procurement approval in many cases.
3) Commit appetite: For pilot phase finance is unlikely to sign 12-month commits. If we see SLOs and measurable cost predictability after pilot (Q1), we can consider a 6–12 month committed pool.

Open items: 
- Can you provide a one-page SOW template + high-level MPA term highlights?
- If we go on-card pilot, what are the per-token cost ranges we should expect for hosted vs dedicated versus private evaluation?

Appreciate the attach — will review and come back with any compliance questions.

—Alicia
Alicia Grant | Head of Technical Procurement, StatelyPay
alicia@statelypay.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Grant <alicia@statelypay.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement check — Redwood fit

Thanks for the fast turn, Alicia — helpful. I’m attaching a short MPA term-sheet and a pricing summary (see attachments) to make procurement review faster. High-level answers below so you can share with ProcureOps: 

- SOW / MPA: attached MPA-term-sheet.xlsx shows standard Redwood commercial terms; SOW template included in the doc — we can adapt for pilot scope (hours, success metrics, runbook).

- Pricing ranges (very high-level ballpark rates for initial planning):
  * Hosted (on-demand): $0.003 — $0.015 per token (depends on model family and streaming vs batch) — good for fast pilot and no infra commit.
  * Dedicated (reserved capacity): equivalent unit cost often 30–50% lower at commit levels; requires a monthly reserved spend commitment (we can propose a staged commit starting month 3).
  * Private (VPC/on-prem): enterprise-priced, includes license + ops fee; typically negotiated (we can supply an indicative TCO spreadsheet).

- Marketplace: we are listed on AWS Marketplace for our hosted/consumption SKU — covers card and invoice paths; Dedicated purchase via Marketplace depends on procurement rules (some customers buy UI/consumption via Marketplace and then add a Dedicated contract). Link: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/B0CEXAMPLE

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share the two attachments (MPA-term-sheet.xlsx, redwood-pricing-summary-nov2026.pdf) for ProcureOps to review.
2) If ProcureOps confirms PO path, I’ll introduce our contracts lead and solutions engineer to draft a pilot SOW (timeline: 1 week to initial draft).
3) If you prefer card pilot: we can enable a hosted project within 24–48 hours and supply a short onboarding runbook.

Ben, looping you in to confirm the pricing bands and whether we should propose a 3-month staged commit for the Dedicated option as an intermediate concession. Monica — can you own contracts intro if Alicia confirms PO path?

Best,
Jordan
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement check — Redwood fit

Jordan / Monica — quick pricing confirmation and recommended ask: 

- Confirmed bands roughly match what I sent earlier; for StatelyPay size I’d recommend proposing:
  * Pilot: hosted on-demand (card) — capped budget $8k with usage alerts.
  * Short-term (post-pilot): 3-month Dedicated staged commit (start at 30% of expected peak) — we can offer 20% discount off hosted list for that staged commit.
  * Long-term: 12-month Dedicated commit only if they can provide a forecast within 60 days after pilot.

- Marketplace note: AWS Marketplace SKU is available for the hosted consumption path and will speed PO approvals for some finance teams. For Dedicated we can offer an invoice/PO route with standard MPA.

I attached the MPA and pricing summary to Jordan’s thread — happy to jump on a quick call with ProcureOps to walk numbers if helpful.

—Ben
